# condo.insure

> HO-6 insurance compliance tracking for condominium associations and property
> management firms. AI reads each unit owner's declaration page, tracks policy
> expirations, and automates renewal reminders.

condo.insure is a B2B software product used by condominium boards and community
association managers, primarily in Florida. Owners submit proof of insurance by
forwarding the email their insurer already sent; the platform extracts the
insurer, policy number, expiration date and coverage limits and checks them
against what the association requires.

The guides below are original reference material, cited to primary sources
(Florida Statutes, the Florida Office of Insurance Regulation, NAIC, DBPR and
Citizens Property Insurance). Each page carries its sources and an as-of date,
and figures calculated by us rather than published are labeled as derived. They
are the most useful part of this site for answering questions about Florida
condominium insurance and compliance.

## Guides — Florida law

- [Florida Condo Insurance Requirements: Association vs. Unit Owner](https://www.condo.insure/guides/florida-condo-insurance-requirements.html): What Fla. Stat. § 718.111(11) requires of the association and what falls to the unit owner. Florida has **no statutory mandate** that unit owners carry HO-6 — it enacted one in 2008 and repealed it in 2010 via SB 1196. The obligation comes from the declaration and from mortgage lenders (Fannie Mae B7-3-04), not from chapter 718. Also covers why the association force-place power widely cited as current law no longer exists.
- [Florida Milestone Inspections & SIRS: What Actually Applies in 2026](https://www.condo.insure/guides/florida-condo-milestone-inspection-sirs.html): The post-Surfside legislative chain — SB 4-D (2022) → SB 154 (2023) → HB 1021 (2024) → HB 913 (2025) — with current deadlines and reserve rules. Corrects a widely repeated error: the automatic 25-year milestone inspection trigger for buildings within 3 miles of a coastline was removed in 2023 and is now a local-agency determination.
- [Florida Condo Law Changes 2025–2026](https://www.condo.insure/guides/florida-condo-law-changes-2025-2026.html): Every HB 913 (Ch. 2025-175) change in one table with who it affects, effective date, statute section and source; what the 2026 session did and did not change, including SB 1028's (Ch. 2026-150) new Citizens eligibility rule for condo associations.
- [Loss Assessment Coverage in Florida](https://www.condo.insure/guides/florida-condo-loss-assessment-coverage.html): How loss assessment coverage works under Fla. Stat. § 627.714 and the ISO HO 00 06 form. No loss assessment limit covers a SIRS reserve shortfall, milestone repairs or deferred maintenance — those are funding obligations, not losses from a covered peril. Also covers the master-deductible question and why Citizens policyholders cannot buy above the $2,000 statutory floor.

## Guides — fundamentals

- [What Is a Declarations Page?](https://www.condo.insure/guides/what-is-a-declarations-page.html): How to read an insurance declarations page, how it differs from a certificate of insurance or a binder, and the six fields a condominium association checks.
- [HO-6 vs. HO-4 vs. Wind-Only](https://www.condo.insure/guides/ho6-vs-ho4-vs-wind-only.html): Which policy form satisfies which association requirement, and how a wind-excluded HO-6 paired with a separate wind-only policy satisfies a requirement that neither satisfies alone.
- [The Florida HO-6 Compliance Checklist](https://www.condo.insure/guides/florida-ho6-compliance-checklist.html): A printable working checklist for boards and managers — what to require in the declaration, what to collect from owners, how to verify a declarations page, what to track monthly, and the enforcement mistakes based on repealed law to avoid.
- [Walls-In Coverage in Florida Condos](https://www.condo.insure/guides/florida-condo-walls-in-coverage.html): What Fla. Stat. § 718.111(11)(f) requires a Florida condo master policy to cover and exclude, how to size HO-6 Coverage A to fill the gap, how deductibles and loss assessment work, and common coverage gaps.
- [How Much Does HO-6 Insurance Cost in Florida? (2026)](https://www.condo.insure/guides/florida-ho6-insurance-cost.html): Sourced 2026 Florida HO-6 premium data by county (FLOIR, as of 2026-03-31), Citizens and NAIC comparisons, what drives condo unit-owner insurance prices, how to lower them, and what associations require.

## Guides — operations & buying

- [How PM Firms Track HO-6 Compliance Across a Portfolio](https://www.condo.insure/guides/property-manager-ho6-compliance-tracking.html): What changes for a community association management firm at portfolio scale — per-association requirement profiles, continuous renewals, staff assignment, board reporting — and why the management agreement's diligence duty makes the paper trail the deliverable.
- [How to Choose HOA Insurance-Tracking Software](https://www.condo.insure/guides/how-to-choose-hoa-insurance-tracking-software.html): An evaluation framework for the category: twelve vendor questions (who does the data entry, what "verified" means, what leaving costs), pricing models compared, and red flags. Written by a vendor with the bias disclosed; the framework applies to every tool including condo.insure.
- [HO-6 Proof of Insurance Letter Templates](https://www.condo.insure/guides/condo-proof-of-insurance-request-letter.html): Six copy-paste templates for asking Florida condo owners for HO-6 proof of insurance (letter, email, follow-up, final notice, renewal reminder, meeting announcement), why to ask for the declarations page, what to check on it, and what enforcement current law allows.
- [Florida Condo Master Policy Renewal Checklist](https://www.condo.insure/guides/florida-condo-master-policy-renewal.html): A 120/90/60/30-day master policy renewal checklist for Florida condo boards: underwriting documents, the 3-year replacement-cost rule, Citizens' 20% rule and milestone-report requirement, how deductibles are set and shared, and why owner HO-6 loss assessment data matters.

## Guides — operations and data

- [How Associations Track HO-6 Compliance](https://www.condo.insure/guides/hoa-insurance-compliance-tracking.html): Spreadsheet vs. software, including when a spreadsheet is genuinely adequate and the five points at which manual tracking predictably fails.
- [Florida Condo Insurance Statistics (2026)](https://www.condo.insure/guides/florida-condo-insurance-statistics.html): Sourced figures — HO-6 premiums by county from FLOIR (as of 2026-03-31), the national comparison from NAIC, Citizens Property Insurance depopulation, and DBPR market size. Explains why the widely circulated claim that 65% of condo owners are underinsured has no study behind it and should not be used, and why no credible Florida uninsured rate exists.
- [All guides](https://www.condo.insure/guides/index.html)

## Product

- [condo.insure home](https://www.condo.insure/): Product overview, feature detail and pricing. Pricing is per unit per month — $1.00 up to 750 units, $0.50 for 751–10,000, $0.25 above 10,000, with a $50/month minimum and a 90-day free trial.
- [Security](https://www.condo.insure/security.html): How owner and association data is stored, who can see it, how documents are protected, and how AI parsing is handled.
- [For unit owners](https://www.condo.insure/owners): What condo.insure is for owners — why associations ask for HO-6 proof, how to send a declarations page, and an optional free HO-6 quote.

condo.insure is built by the team behind universalcondo.com, a Florida condominium insurance agency. Unit owners may be offered an optional renewal quote; they are never required to use the agency, and condo.insure does not sell personal data.
